gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a MacBook Air with M3 drives only one external display while its lid is open, which is how an attached extender is always used (Apple says the second display goes dark when the lid opens), while M4 and M5 Airs drive two, so the number of screens on the box is not the number a student's Air can extend to.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides' 15-best page (cited), Macworld's portable monitors for Mac (cited) and the 2025 itechguides page's listing of the same products. Macworld says only that plain M1 and M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo are 'limited to connecting just a single monitor' and that the Trio 3 Pro needs Mobile Pixels' software on them. It never mentions M3, the lid-open condition, or that M4 and M5 Airs drive two. itechguides says MacBook compatibility 'cannot be reduced to yes or no' and gives no count for any chip. TechRepublic (cited) returned HTTP 403, so I could not check it. None of these pages turns '2 screens' or '3 screens' into the number of screens a given Air actually extends.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's 'one added screen' advice, but for a specific reason. On a base M1, M2 or M3 MacBook Air, the most common student Mac, an attached extender is used with the lid open, so the laptop drives one external screen natively. A dual or triple extender adds only one extended screen unless the maker's display driver (DisplayLink-style) is installed. Mobile Pixels' own product record says this for the Trio 3 Pro. I did not open that page today; see unsourced. A single attached screen therefore wins for M1–M3 Air owners. The Duex Max DS is the one we link, and its record lists a 14.1-inch 1080p screen on one USB-C cable when the port has DisplayPort Alt Mode, also not re-opened today. A two-screen extender is a fair pick only for M4 or M5 Air owners, or Windows laptops with two video-capable USB-C ports. The page should ask which chip the shopper's MacBook has before recommending any dual or triple model. I could not source FOPO's video path today, so the FOPO S1 and S7 rows still need it before they can be placed.

findings.label: External displays, MacBook Air with M3, lid open vs closed
findings.value: Two external displays only with the lid closed; opening the lid with both connected makes 'the secondary external display … go dark or disconnect'
findings.source_title: Use dual monitors with your MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M3 chip - Apple Support
findings.note: Lid-closed dual-display mode also needs an external keyboard and mouse or trackpad, external power, and macOS Sonoma 14.3 or later on the Air. An attached extender is used with the lid open, so an M3 Air extends to one added screen natively.

findings.label: External displays, MacBook Air with M4 and M5
findings.value: Up to two external displays at once in addition to the built-in display; closing the lid does not raise the count
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Air - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's page covers only M4 and M5 Airs. Two with the lid open means a dual extender can extend both screens on these chips, provided each screen gets a native video path.
